intent.raw: Set up a dispatch spec to research feasibility of using DCB to prove saga correctness using DomainSpec TAXONOMY.md and RELATIONSHIPS.md, with a possible prebuilt structure or TypeScript.
intent.objective: Evaluate whether DCB can support saga correctness proofs or claim-acceptance freshness for DomainSpec saga models, and choose a small language or harness path for the first toy proof.
intent.operator_sentence: Use DomainSpec taxonomy and relationships to derive saga proof obligations, compare DCB against simpler freshness strategies, choose a modeling language, then hand off a toy saga correctness pilot.

items.label: DCB saga boundary
items.description: Build the strongest DCB-shaped account of saga correctness claim freshness.

items.label: Alternatives
items.description: Hold the saga-correctness problem fixed and compare rerun, hashes, snapshots, and certificates against DCB.

items.label: Language tournament
items.description: Compare TypeScript, TLA+, Alloy, and Lean for a minimal saga proof or bounded witness.

subagent_strategy.trigger: Saga correctness crosses taxonomy, relationship graph, DCB freshness semantics, language choice, and adversarial alternatives.
subagent_strategy.explanation: Role-bound sibling lanes can explore the DCB hypothesis, alternatives, formal model fit, and TypeScript harness fit without collapsing into a single favored framing.
context: DomainSpec v2 research uses the two-lane discipline.
Prior DCB research found DCB valuable mainly for non-rerunnable and concurrent correctness claims.
Saga correctness spans multiple bounded contexts and typed relationship edges.

roles.purpose: Derive saga proof obligations from DomainSpec meta-concepts and relationship edges.
Build the strongest DCB read-set, append-condition, and freshness model for accepting saga correctness claims.
Compare content hashes, rerun-before-use, snapshot diff, and certificate binding against DCB.
Assess TLA+, Alloy, and Lean as proof or bounded-model surfaces for saga correctness.
Assess a TypeScript DomainSpec saga DSL and property-test harness as the first executable structure.

subagent_strategy.permission_prompt: Run the DCB saga correctness research lanes as sibling subagents, then join their receipts into LANE-RECEIPTS.md?

agents.residue: orchestrates signature, compensation semantics, participant representation, and evidence vocabulary need synthesis
DCB must stay a freshness/concurrency wrapper, not a behavioral proof engine
classify deterministic/rerunnable facts separately from non-rerunnable DCB facts
TLA+/PlusCal is the formal promotion path if temporal behavior is hard; Alloy if graph completeness is hard
TypeScript gives a bounded witness, not a proof; implement SagaSpec -> validateGraph -> enumerateRuns -> acceptClaim

steps.name: Build the saga taxonomy and relationship obligation frame
convergence_criteria: The frame maps Saga, Operation, Rule, Policy, Event, State Machine, Entity, Interface, and Mapping to proof obligations.
The frame names every relationship edge needed for the toy saga.
stop_conditions: Flag if an obligation depends on a relationship type not present in RELATIONSHIPS.md.

steps.name: Run DCB, alternatives, formal-model, and TypeScript harness lanes

capability_metadata.validation_note: Dispatch-spec recommends the sibling lane shape but does not execute subagents.

convergence_criteria: DCB lane distinguishes proof of saga behavior from freshness of proof acceptance.
Alternatives lane holds the saga-correctness problem fixed and proposes non-DCB solutions.
Language lanes return a concrete first-pilot recommendation, not only a preference.
stop_conditions: Block execution if subagent lanes are not authorized by the operator.
Flag any lane receipt that lacks path-cited evidence.

steps.name: Choose the first modeling structure

capability_metadata.validation_note: Used to compare modeling-language options and record the human-gated choice.

convergence_criteria: TypeScript is preferred only if it can produce a useful bounded witness or property-test harness.
TLA+ is preferred if temporal saga behavior is the central proof target.
Alloy is preferred if taxonomy and relationship completeness are the central proof target.
Lean is deferred unless the theorem is small enough to state and check without blocking the pilot.
stop_conditions: Ask for a decision if no candidate dominates on proof signal, implementation cost, and repo fit.

steps.name: Design the toy saga correctness proof or bounded witness

capability_metadata.validation_note: Used here as a planning target for a later bounded toy run.

convergence_criteria: The toy includes at least one non-rerunnable fact such as a waiver, human approval, agent verdict, or external receipt.
The toy includes one stale saga-correctness claim rejected by DCB-style freshness.
The toy includes one saga behavioral obligation checked by the selected model or harness.
stop_conditions: Downgrade DCB to content-hash or rerun-before-use if all facts in the toy are deterministic and cheap to recompute.

steps.name: Synthesize the DCB saga correctness feasibility verdict
convergence_criteria: Verdict separates DCB as proof engine, DCB as freshness wrapper, and the selected modeling language as proof surface.
Verdict names promotion-candidate, borrow-carefully, analogy-only, or block decisions per claim.
stop_conditions: Block any synthesis that claims DCB proves saga behavior without an independent model or executable witness.

steps.name: Prepare the next task-session handoff
stop_conditions: Do not mutate DomainSpec templates, validators, taxonomy, relationships, or generated registries from this research dispatch.

gates.condition: The route may use TAXONOMY.md and RELATIONSHIPS.md as explanatory sources, but DS-D1 and DS-D2 remain the normative authority if wording differs.
Every verdict must distinguish proving saga behavior from accepting fresh evidence about that proof.
The DCB pilot must include at least one non-rerunnable fact or concurrent acceptance race; otherwise it should downgrade to content hash, snapshot diff, or rerun-before-use.
The model choice must compare TypeScript, TLA+, Alloy, and Lean against proof signal, repo fit, adoption cost, and toy feasibility.
Research outputs cannot change templates, validators, taxonomy, relationships, ontology, glossary, sigils, spells, or registry behavior without a later approved task-session.

boundaries.contract: This dispatch writes only research, lane receipts, synthesis, and handoff artifacts under the DCB saga correctness research folder.
DCB may guard freshness of accepted proof evidence; the selected model or harness owns the behavioral proof or bounded witness.

authority.execution: future task-session or approved subagent fanout
authority.promotion: DomainSpec v2 owner after later decision

receipts.producer: future task-session or approved research fanout

promotion_splits.target: DomainSpec canonical templates, validators, taxonomy, relationships, ontology, glossary, sigils, spells, or registry behavior
promotion_splits.rule: requires later approved task-session and owner review

promotion_guardrails: This dispatch is research planning only.
Template, validator, taxonomy, relationship, registry, ontology, glossary, sigil, or spell changes require a later approved task-session.
DCB evidence may not be reported as a saga behavioral proof unless a selected model or executable witness supports the claim.
